searches.note: Twenty five searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, and three left unspent. One was restricted to the Consejo Regulador DO Rueda's own domain (dorueda.com: its back label note and its present wines page) and is read as primary through its summary. The rest went to the open web with the author's sources blocked where they would only have repeated themselves (the houses' own domains, Spanish Wine Lover, Skurnik, Enterwine, Decántalo, Wine Spectator, Decanter, Wikipedia, the Consejos by turns). The four shared searches are DO Rueda's order of 1980, its label rules (two) and DO Toro's order of 1987; numanthia's count of two leaves out the Toro order, which serves Numanthia and Fariña alike. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the governing bodies (the Consejo Regulador DO Rueda, the order of 1987 for Toro in the BOE and ITACyL's copy) and to independent accounts of each house's dates, then to importers' and merchants' sheets for the making and to tasting notes for the glass, with the author's sources blocked so that an independent account would show.

Where the sources corrected the record it was set right with its source (the label rules of Rueda, the DO Toro recognised rather than created, the Fariña presidency, the glass of four wines); where a detail rested on one account or none it was cut (the green back label, gravel and bush vines at Limousin, white fruit and infused herbs, black cherry and toast at Termanthia, cocoa at Pintia, the six bodegas, liquorice and balsamic at Fariña, the Crianza's years in bottle, a Colegiata red).

Claims of a house's own dates and methods stand, hedged as its account where they are its telling. Sources whose title or address names a living person (a trade profile of the Fariña son, an importer's page) were met in the results but never cited; the fragment's sources were changed only where the record now rests on the refuter's (the Consejo's wines page for Decanter on Peynaud), and every new source is listed per record under extraSources.

tested: The arrival in Rueda, 1972 and Peynaud: Wikipedia (the bodega in Rueda in 1972, the DO in 1980) and Wine-Searcher (the first Verdejo whites of 1972, Peynaud as consultant, the house's part in the DO of 1980) bear out the house's 1972 and the consultant; the Consejo's around 1970 is the author's, kept hedged. Confirmed.

Peynaud's dates, 29 June 1912 to 18 July 2004: World of Fine Wine, the Encyclopédie Universalis and wein.plus, with the author's Wikipedia and Decanter. Confirmed; the record names him once with his dates, as the brief asks.

DO Rueda of 12 January 1980 by an order of the Ministry of Agriculture, the first of Castilla y León: Interempresas, the Mancomunidad de Tierras de Medina and a bodega's history page, with the author's Consejo. Confirmed.

The label rules: the regulation of 2011 on the Consejo's site gives Rueda Verdejo at 85 per cent and plain Rueda at 50 per cent Verdejo; the Consejo's older note gives the green label to 85 per cent Verdejo and the orange to 50; its present wines page gives the green label to still wines of three quarters main grapes and a quarter secondary. The Codex's region record (reviewed in the records edition against the governing body) holds no Verdejo floor for a plain Rueda since August 2024. The trap and the label line were set right and the colour cut.

The making: the Vintus 2024 sheet and the Shaw-Ross sheets of 2019 and 2022 give steel, one to two months on the lees, the lees moved weekly with nitrogen, bottling between January and March, Verdejo alone. Confirmed; the grapes now say Verdejo alone.

The glass: the house's notes through Wine.com (2017, 2022, 2025: fennel, white flowers, aniseed, fresh grass, smooth and fresh, a slightly bitter finish typical of the variety) and Vinous for 2024 (fennel, orange blossom); grapefruit in none. Rewritten.

Limousin: Tanino Wines, Enterwine and Decántalo give Verdejo from old vines on the highest terraces of the Duero, fermented in 600 litre French oak barrels and aged on its lees, Gran Vino de Rueda; one merchant's critic gives foudres and concrete. The author's barrel fermentation stands; gravel and bush vines cut.

Sauvignon Blanc brought to Rueda in 1974: several merchants and an encyclopaedia entry repeat the house's line; kept as the house's account. The serve, 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, is the Codex's reference for a light white; the house rules hold (no living name, no price or score, British, no dash).

tested: Founded 1994, the first vintage at Nava del Rey in rented premises and on the market in 1996, the cellar at La Seca in 2000: Grandes Pagos de España, AECOC Trade, Vinoteca Collado, Vila Viniteca and Lavinia. Vila Viniteca adds the founder's tasting of a young Rueda in 1992, which fits the story's Frenchman who had fallen for Verdejo. Confirmed.

Quinta San Diego, Quinta Clarisa and Quinta Apolonia: Selectus Wines and others give the estate named after a son, the rosé of 2000 named for the younger daughter and the Verdejo of 2002 for the elder. Confirmed; AECOC Trade gives the first plots of the estate planted in 1999, one source, left out.

The making: La Cava de Piñero, Casa Pablo and other listings of the 2023 give ten months on the lees in French oak and at least five months in bottle, spontaneous fermentation, each plot fermented and aged apart, hand picking on the organic Quinta San Diego; one gives barrels of 300 litres and none 500. Confirmed but for the 500 litres, which rest on the house's sheet and stay.
The grapes: listings disagree between Verdejo alone and a small share of other grapes beside it, so the record now says all or nearly all.

Organic since 2010: Vinoteca Collado. Confirmed. The serve (10 to 13 degrees Celsius, a white Burgundy glass) is the Codex's reference for a full white. The house rules hold: the founder, his son, his daughters by their given names, the technical director and the architect are never named in prose (the daughters' names are the wines' own).

changed.why: Listings of the 2023 differ, some giving Verdejo alone and some a small share of other grapes (the author's 2024 sheet does the same), so the small share is not one vintage's alone.

tested: Founded 1998 by the Eguren family of Rioja, the cellar at Valdefinjas, the sale to LVMH in 2008: LVMH's own maison page, Grandes Pagos de España, El Español and a company register (13 February 2008, through Moët Hennessy). Confirmed. Wine-Searcher adds a living importer to the founding, not in the record.

The making: Gourmet Hunters, Enterwine and The Drinks Business give about twenty months in French oak, most of it new (eighty new and twenty used in one, up to twenty one months in another), fermentation in small French oak vats or truncated cone barrels, and hand destemming grape by grape. Confirmed.

The others: Numanthia sixteen months in French barrels of 225 and 400 litres, about sixty per cent new for 2020 (Enterwine); Termes sixteen months with a fifth new for 2018. Confirmed; Termes's far less new oak stands.

The DO's order of 29 May 1987, published on 2 June 1987: the BOE's summary and ITACyL's copy of the order, which also requires at least three quarters Tinta de Toro in a red and repealed an order of 1985. Confirmed; created set right to recognised.

The rest: Numantia's twenty years against Rome is told as the house tells it; the ungrafted vines of more than a century rest on the house's page with Decántalo; the serve follows the Codex for a full red against the house's 14 to 15. The house rules hold: no Eguren is named; the region record's cult prices are not repeated.

tested: The first vintage of 2001: Bodeboca gives the first harvest of 2001, sold in 2004, the vineyards bought between 1997 and 2000; Gourmet Hunters the old vines on rounded stones; the DO Toro's own register lists the bodega. Confirmed; founded stays empty.

The making: Bebevino, Lecole Gourmet and other listings of the 2020 give twelve months in barrels, about seven tenths French and three tenths American, the malolactic wholly in wood, Tinta de Toro alone, and, on the producer's own copy, amphorae beside the barrels and at least a year in bottle. Confirmed.

The Vaccaean city and its patrons: the University of Valladolid's own notice gives a new agreement with the Tempos Vega Sicilia group, the tenth in thirty years, and the group's head a member of the centre's board; the Fundación Palarq gives the Pintia project of 1999 with the group among its partners. Confirmed.

The glass: no note read gives plum, black cherry or cocoa; Berry Bros. (2016) gives cherry, black raspberry, potpourri, liquorice and woodsmoke, Bodeboca (2014) candied fruit, prunes, toast and withered violets, and (2021) power, density and more freshness than the alcohol suggests. Rewritten.

The rest: the Álvarez purchase of Vega Sicilia in April 1982 agrees with wave one's record; the serve and the fifteen years rest on the house's sheets. The house rules hold: the family is named as a family, its head never.

changed.was: Ripe plum and black cherry with cocoa and toast from the barrel; full and juicy, silky in texture, with polished tannin and fresh lift for so warm a place.
changed.now: Cherry, black raspberry and prune with violet, liquorice and a toasty, smoky note from the barrel; powerful and dense yet juicy and silky, with fruity tannin and more freshness than its warmth suggests.
changed.why: The author marked plum, black cherry and cocoa as his own words; the notes read give cherry, black raspberry, liquorice and woodsmoke (Berry Bros. for 2016), prune, toast and violet (Bodeboca for 2014), very fruity tannin (the house's sheet for 2018) and more freshness than the alcohol suggests (Bodeboca for 2021). Cocoa is in none of them and is cut.

tested: Founded 1942 at Casaseca de las Chanas by a couple from Porto de Sanabria, as Bodegas Porto after their home village, in cellars dug into limestone: Vinopremier, AECOC Trade, Entrée Cuvée and the Diario de Castilla y León (quoting the family). Confirmed; the founders are described, never named, since no dates were found.

The 1970s: Viajes y Vinos and a trade profile give the son bringing the harvest forward by almost a month and the reds from about 17 degrees to 13 or 14, and the first Colegiata wines of the decade aged in American oak. Confirmed; the house's 16 or 17 stays hedged as its account.

The son first president of the Consejo of the DO Toro: Vivir el Vino and a trade profile, with the house and Enterwine. Confirmed; the order of 1987 had the Ministry name the president on the Consejo's proposal, so became replaces elected. The six bodegas rest on the house alone and are cut.

Gran Colegiata Original: Sembra, Destilerías Bonet, Smartbites and others give a Reserva of Tinta de Toro alone, eighteen months in barrels, American oak in most sheets (one says French), ungrafted vines over sixty years (one gives 100 to 140). Confirmed; no page read names the Burgundy bottle, which is hedged.

The others and the glass: the house's wines page gives Fariña Crianza twelve months in French oak from ungrafted vines over forty years and Colegiata Blanco, Malvasía alone and unoaked; Guía Peñín (2020) and Decanter (2017) give toast, cocoa, ripe black fruit, full body, soft tannin and poise. Set right as listed.

The DO's rules: the order of 29 May 1987 (ITACyL's copy) requires three quarters Tinta de Toro in a red; the Reserva's thirty six months with twelve in barrel follow the national law the Consejo applies. The house rules hold: the son and the Consejo's later presidents are never named; a guide's score met in the results is not used.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json (Belondrade and Fariña as the names of houses, which a house keeps, and Lurton as the word of a wine's name). The author's report says the Vega Sicilia family's head is already on people.json: the refuter found no Álvarez entry there, so it is listed here. The founder's daughters are met only by their given names, which are the names of the wines Quinta Apolonia and Quinta Clarisa, and his son Diego by the estate's name; none is a name to refuse. Long dead or undated and described, never named: Salvador Fariña and Tomasa López, the founders of 1942 (named in a merchant's blog, no dates found); the founder of Marqués de Riscal of 1858 and the master winemaker of the 1860s. Émile Peynaud (1912 to 2004) is named with his dates, borne out by World of Fine Wine and the Encyclopédie Universalis.
swapNote: No swap was proposed by the author, and the refuter proposes none. Marqués de Riscal stands as the Rioja house's Rueda arm with a Rueda wine, the plan's intent, and the 1972 of the region record is borne out by three accounts; Belondrade, Numanthia, Pintia and Bodegas Fariña are real houses of their denominations, each making the wine its record tells, which independent accounts bear out (Grandes Pagos de España, LVMH, Bodeboca, the DO Toro's register, the merchants of Gran Colegiata Original).
planNotes: marques-de-riscal: answered. The label of the years taught reads Marqués de Riscal Verdejo under DO Rueda (the sheets), the plan's words kept as the wine's name; 1972 by the house, Wikipedia and Wine-Searcher, around 1970 by the Consejo; the consultant Peynaud by the Consejo, Wikipedia and Wine-Searcher, his dates by World of Fine Wine and the Encyclopédie Universalis. The why's cold fermented Verdejo stands.

belondrade: answered. 1994 by Grandes Pagos de España, Vila Viniteca and Vinology; neither founder named; DO Rueda on every listing read. The why's French couple, one of them of the Lurton family, is not borne out by the refuter's sources, which name the founder alone: the read together agent may set the why to a Frenchman whose wine joins his name to Lurton.
numanthia: answered. Termanthia the head wine, Numanthia the middle and Termes the entry, kept straight; the sale of 2008 by LVMH, El Español and a company register; no Eguren named.

pintia: answered in part. The first vintage of 2001 by Bodeboca with the author's three; the estate's founding unsettled (vineyards bought from 1997 to 2000, the bodega dated 2001 by Bodeboca, 1995 to 1997 elsewhere), so founded stays empty and the why's first vintage 2001 stands.

farina: answered. 1942 at Casaseca de las Chanas by Vinopremier, AECOC Trade and the Diario de Castilla y León; the presidency of the first Consejo by Vivir el Vino and a trade profile with the house; the bottling taught is Gran Colegiata Original, a Reserva by every listing read. The why stands.
